input.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
input.rationale: Section 28 sits at our preferred position: New York law governs the Agreement and each dispute arising from it (28.1), and the state and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction with irrevocable submission and a venue/forum-non-conveniens waiver (28.2). The only other-court carve-out is the customary one for temporary injunctive relief to protect confidential information or IP, which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. There is no arbitration clause anywhere in the document; 28.3's pre-filing executive escalation is a short good-faith step that expressly does not delay urgent relief or a limitations-period filing, so it does not displace the court forum. No redline needed.
